description: CRISPRArchitect v2 benchmark dataset with 30 curated cases from ClinVar and Ensembl. All coordinates are on GRCh38. Each case includes biological rationale for the expected editing modality, enabling evaluation of consequence-aware strategy ranking. v1.1: Genomic positions corrected via Ensembl REST API CDS-to-genomic mapping (/map/cds and /vep/human/hgvs endpoints) for all single-variant cases with known cDNA positions.
coordinate_verification: Positions verified using Ensembl REST API v112+ /map/cds/{transcript_id} and /vep/human/hgvs endpoints. Reference alleles confirmed against GRCh38 forward strand sequence via /sequence/region. For reverse strand genes (HBB, TSC1), ref_allele in dataset matches the CDS/HGVS convention (complement of forward strand).

rationale: Nonsense mutation p.Arg304Ter: C>T on coding strand means G>A on template strand
ABE correction A>G on template strand restores Arg codon
Clean C>T transition is the canonical ABE target class
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000043587; position verified via Ensembl VEP CDS-to-genomic mapping (GRCh38)

rationale: Missense p.Gly551Asp: G>A transition at a well-characterized CF-causing locus
ABE can correct A>G to restore wild-type glycine codon
G551D is an FDA-approved ivacaftor target, validating clinical relevance
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000007107; rs75527207; position verified via Ensembl VEP (GRCh38)

rationale: Splice donor G>A variant disrupts canonical GT splice signal
ABE correction A>G restores splice donor consensus sequence
Splice site variants are high-priority ABE targets due to precise correction
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000017070; COL7A1 splice donor variants are recurrent in DEB

rationale: Missense variant A>G: correction requires C>T edit on coding strand
CBE can install the corrective C>T change to restore wild-type allele
Single transition amenable to cytosine base editor
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000051065; BRCA2 missense classified as likely pathogenic; position verified via Ensembl CDS mapping (GRCh38)

rationale: Nonsense mutation p.Arg320Ter: C>T creates premature stop codon
ABE correction of A>G on antisense strand restores Arg codon
RB1 Arg>Ter mutations are the most common class in retinoblastoma
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000012146; recurrent CGA>TGA nonsense in RB1; position verified via Ensembl VEP (GRCh38)

rationale: Nonsense mutation p.Arg505Ter: C>T transition in CGA codon
ABE correction A>G restores arginine, a recurrent hotspot in TSC2
Clean transition amenable to ABE without bystander risk
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000012476; recurrent CGA>TGA nonsense hotspot in TSC2; position verified via Ensembl CDS mapping (GRCh38)

rationale: Missense T>C transition: correction requires C>T on coding strand
CBE can install the corrective edit to restore wild-type residue
FBN1 missense mutations in cbEGF domains are a major class of Marfan-causing variants
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000042805; FBN1 missense in calcium-binding EGF-like domain

rationale: Sickle mutation p.Glu7Val: A>T TRANSVERSION (not a transition)
Neither ABE nor CBE can correct transversion mutations
Base editing should be rejected; PE or HDR required for precise correction
This is a critical negative control for the base editing classifier
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000015333; HBB c.20A>T (rs334) is the canonical sickle cell variant; position verified via Ensembl VEP at chr11:5227002 (GRCh38, reverse strand: genomic fwd T, CDS ref A). This case tests that the pipeline correctly rejects base editing for transversions.

rationale: Nonsense p.Gly542Ter: G>T transversion creates premature stop
Transversion cannot be corrected by ABE or CBE
Prime editing can install precise T>G correction via pegRNA
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000007108; CFTR G542X is the second most common CF nonsense mutation worldwide; position verified via Ensembl VEP (GRCh38)

rationale: Nonsense mutation via C>A transversion in NF1
Transversion precludes base editing correction
PE can precisely install the A>C reversion
cases.notes: NF1 transversion variant; PE is the preferred DSB-free approach; position verified via Ensembl CDS mapping (GRCh38)

rationale: 4bp deletion causing frameshift in BRCA2 exon 7
Small deletion is within PE RT-template capacity (up to ~40bp insertion/deletion)
Base editing cannot install insertions; PE is preferred
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000051587; recurrent small deletion in BRCA2

rationale: 2bp deletion causing frameshift in DMD
Small deletion is within PE design capacity
Prime editing inserts the missing AG dinucleotide via pegRNA RT template
cases.notes: DMD small deletion; hemizygous in males simplifies editing genotyping

rationale: In-frame 3bp deletion removing one amino acid from polycystin-1
Small in-frame deletion is ideal PE target: precise reinsertion via RT template
No frameshift, but functional domain disruption is pathogenic
cases.notes: PKD1 in-frame deletion; PE reinstates the missing codon

rationale: 1bp insertion causing frameshift in COL7A1
Small insertion (1bp) is well within PE capacity
PE deletes the inserted G to restore reading frame
cases.notes: COL7A1 small insertion; recurrent frameshift class in DEB

rationale: 2bp deletion in TSC1 causing frameshift and premature termination
Small deletion within PE RT-template capacity
PE reinstates the CT dinucleotide to restore reading frame
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000012391; TSC1 frameshift deletion; position verified via Ensembl VEP at chr9:132906052-132906053 (GRCh38, reverse strand gene, fwd strand ref CG)

rationale: Whole-exon deletion: too large for PE (>40bp capacity)
Exon skipping strategy via dual-guide flanking deletion or HDR-based exon reinsertion
Base editing irrelevant: not a point mutation

rationale: 70bp deletion exceeds PE RT-template length capacity (~40bp)

rationale: F508del (c.1521_1523delCTT) is the most common CF mutation worldwide (~70%)
3bp in-frame deletion: PE can insert CTT via RT template
HDR with ssODN is also feasible given the small size
Base editing cannot install insertions
cases.notes: ClinVar VCV000007105; CFTR F508del (rs113993960) at chr7:117559592-117559594 (GRCh38); VCF anchor at 117559591 (ref TCTT, alt T). Position verified via Ensembl CDS mapping and VEP.

cases.disease_context: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (compound heterozygous)
rationale: Two variants on same gene but separated by ~15kb genomic distance
First variant (A>G) is a transition: CBE-correctable
Second variant (T>G) is a transversion: requires PE or HDR
Hybrid strategy (BE for one + PE/HDR for other) avoids dual DSBs
cases.notes: Compound heterozygous BRCA2; hybrid strategy reduces total DSB burden

rationale: Two pathogenic variants in COL7A1 on different alleles
Both are transitions (G>A and C>T), but compound het requires phased editing
Sequential HDR ensures allele-specific correction
Hybrid BE approach possible if allele-specific guides can be designed
cases.notes: Compound het DEB; sequential HDR is the conservative approach for allele-specific correction

cases.disease_context: Malignant hyperthermia / Central core disease (compound heterozygous)
rationale: Two missense variants: G>A and C>T, both are transitions
Both are ABE-correctable (A>G reversion) and CBE-correctable (T>C reversion) respectively
Dual base editing addresses both without any DSBs: safest approach for iPSC
Variants are ~89kb apart, precluding single-donor HDR
cases.notes: RYR1 compound het with two transitions; dual BE is the ideal DSB-free strategy

rationale: Multi-exon deletion (~8kb) far exceeds PE RT-template capacity
Requires HDR with large donor (lssDNA or dsDNA) for exon reinsertion
Not a point mutation, so base editing is not applicable
cases.notes: FBN1 multi-exon deletion; large HDR donor required

rationale: Variant 1 (C>T transition) is ABE-correctable
Variant 2 (G>T transversion) requires PE or HDR
Hybrid approach: ABE for transition + PE/HDR for transversion
Dual BE is rejected because the second variant is a transversion
cases.notes: NF1 compound het with mixed mutation types; tests hybrid strategy selection

rationale: F508del is a 3bp deletion: requires PE or HDR
G551D (G>A) is a transition: ABE-correctable
Hybrid strategy pairs ABE for G551D with PE/HDR for F508del
Dual BE rejected: F508del is a deletion, not a substitution
cases.notes: Common CF compound het; most frequent genotype pairing in CF patients

rationale: Both variants are C>T and G>A transitions
Both are ABE-correctable (reverse the pathogenic transition)
Dual ABE is the safest strategy: zero DSBs, zero donors, single round
Sequential HDR rejected: unnecessary DSB risk when DSB-free option exists
cases.notes: TSC2 compound het with two ABE-amenable transitions; dual BE is optimal

rationale: Variant 1 (C>T) is ABE-correctable transition
Variant 2 is a 2bp deletion requiring PE or HDR
Hybrid BE+PE avoids DSBs entirely
Dual BE rejected: deletion variant cannot be base-edited
cases.notes: DMD with mixed variant types; hybrid BE+PE is the DSB-free optimal

cases.disease_context: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (compound het)
rationale: Variant 1 (G>A) is ABE-correctable transition
Variant 2 (C>A) is a transversion: requires PE or HDR
Hybrid strategy: ABE for the transition, PE/HDR for the transversion
Dual BE rejected: transversion cannot be base-edited
cases.notes: PKD1 compound het; tests correct modality assignment per variant type

rationale: Both variants are transitions (C>T and G>A)
Both can be corrected with ABE (A>G reversion)
Dual ABE is the safest option: no DSBs, no donors
Sequential HDR rejected: unnecessary risk
cases.notes: RB1 bilateral retinoblastoma compound het; dual BE is optimal

rationale: Variants are ~1.9 Mb apart, spanning nearly the entire DMD gene
No single donor template can bridge this distance
Independent correction of each variant is required (sequential or parallel)
Both are transitions: dual ABE is possible if independent guides exist
Tests the pipeline's ability to handle very distant intra-genic variants
cases.notes: DMD is the largest human gene (~2.2 Mb). These variants span nearly its full length, testing the extreme distance handling.

rationale: 5'UTR variant: not in CDS, consequence annotation differs from coding mutations
C>G transversion: base editing cannot correct transversions
PE can install precise G>C correction in non-coding region
Tests the pipeline's handling of non-coding variants and correct rejection of BE for transversions
cases.notes: FMR1 5'UTR variant; tests non-coding variant handling and transversion rejection for BE
